output.title: What subprocessor lists hide in plain sight
output.body:
A subprocessor list is not the whole story. It is a signal that the tool uses other companies to handle part of your data, but it does not tell you whether that setup fits the workflow you actually care about.

If you are a small business owner using SaaS, CRM, invoices, or AI tools, the useful question is simple: which recurring workflow is this tool touching? Customer messages, invoices, and internal docs are not the same thing, even if they all sit in the same dashboard.

Before you give a new tool access, check the exact path your data will take. Who receives it, what it can touch, and whether the workflow needs human approval at the end matter more than the vendor label on the homepage. That is where the hidden work lives. The list on the page is only the cover sheet.

My rule is to start with one recurring workflow and decide whether AI is a fit for that job at all. If the answer is unclear, keep it manual for now. If it is a fit, define the smallest pilot scope you can live with and make sure a human still approves any high-risk step. That keeps the build honest and the scope bounded.
